content:
Maria G: quick thread — proposal for SLO-driven routing + variant fallback DSL. want feedback before i put a prototype in the console UI:

Maria G: problem: higher-tier customers need strict p50/p95 latency targets. when a model variant causes breach we should automatically route to a fallback variant in same region before cross-region failover.

Jay K: +1. question: do we express this as policy objects on the customer, or as per-route configs?

Tom S: per-route seems flexible. but we need an override at tenant level for enterprise SLAs. otherwise teams will forget to set it.

Sophie R: agreed on tenant-level override. also telemetry must include which variant handled request + which fallback triggered (so cost/quality can be attributed).

Maria G: thinking DSL like:
```json
{
  "tier": "enterprise",
  "targets": {"p50_ms": 50, "p95_ms": 200, "availability_pct": 99.9},
  "circuit_breaker": {"window_s": 60, "error_rate_pct": 2, "latency_pctiles": {"p95_ms": 200}},
  "fallback_order": ["fast-quant", "cpu-quant", "regional-variant"],
  "region_failover": true
}
```

Jay K: the cb fields look ok. how do we define "error"? 5xx only? or include soft errors like timeouts and queue-drop?

Tom S: include server error + request_timeout + queue_reject. Those are the common failure modes. mark as "hard_fail" vs "soft_degrade".

Sophie R: also need a grace/backoff: if fallbacks keep failing for 5 minutes, mark route degraded and trigger ops playbook instead of infinite churning.

Lisa O: ops note — for Dedicated customers we need to surface the estimated cost diff when moving to a cheaper variant in the Console. customers will ask. can we include an "estimated_unit_cost" tag in telemetry?

Maria G: yes. telemetry plan: event per decision: {request_id, route, chosen_variant, decision_reason, decision_time_ms, chosen_cost_estimate}. send to routing-prod topic. add sampling for low-tier to save volume.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: please ensure feature flag "slo_routing_v2" is off for prod until canary passes 5k reqs in us-west-2.

Jay K: API debate — option A: RESTy JSON policy resource (POST /policies) that references route ids. Option B: embed policy in route config object. A feels cleaner for re-use; B simpler for UI editing.

Tom S: i prefer A with UI referencing policies. that avoids duplication. we can provide a "clone to route" convenience in console for teams that want per-route tweaks.

Sophie R: UX: show recent rolling window metrics inline in the policy editor (p50/p95/err) and a toggle to preview fallback sequence on sample traffic. also show a simulated cost delta.

Maria G: rollout plan: 1) API + telemetry + basic DSL behind ff. 2) UI editor (read-only) + canary in us-west-2. 3) UI edit + gradual rollout by org size. 4) docs + runbook.

Lisa O: for quotas: ensure circuit-breaker fallback doesn't bypass per-org qps limits. fallback variants still consume quota. otherwise billing/accounting breaks.

Jay K: agree. we should add a field "respect_quotas": true in policy default.

Tom S: testing: integration test where primary variant latency is artificially increased and assert that fallback triggers within 200ms + metric emitted. also add chaos scenario for region down.

Sophie R: monitoring: add alerting rule: if fallback rate > 10% for >10m for enterprise tier, page oncall + notify AE. also expose a dashboard tile with heatmap of fallback triggers by org.

Maria G: @everyone — can folks vote on the API approach? reply with "A" (policy resource) or "B" (embed in route). i wanna lock this by EOD so eng-ux can start mocks.

Jay K: A

Tom S: A

Sophie R: A

Lisa O: A (ops prefers centralized policy)

Maria G: great — majority A. i'll open a PR for the policy API schema and add the telemetry event spec. will tag you all for review.

Maria G: follow-ups: (1) Sophie — can you mock the policy editor preview tile? (2) Jay/Tom — i'll schedule a quick API design sync tomorrow 10am PT. (3) Lisa — i'll add quota constraints to the policy schema.

Sophie R: on it.

Tom S: added to calendar.

Lisa O: i'll draft the ops checklist for when we flip the flag to on.

Maria G: thanks team :thumbsup:
